q: Write in detail the problems of migration and population pressure in Pakistan just after independence?
a: What reactions were left to the economy of Pakistan by these problems? Answers: Migration and Population Problem The Economic condition of a country is duly affected by the increase and decrease in its population. If the population increases constantly, or suddenly it rises to a very high level, the economy of the country will be imbalanced naturally; unless the Government steps forward to meet the new situation. Pakistan faced the same problem just after her existence. Besides the other causes of economic disparity, the migration of Indian Muslims also created a serious disturbance in her economy. Approximately 75 million refugees left India for Pakistan. The population of Pakistan increased rapidly due to such a big migration; which created other economic and social problems. Though the refugees were educated and skilled mostly, the government was not in a position to arrange quickly, food, health, employment, and shelter, for them. Consequently, the economy of Pakistan was badly affected by the migrants.

q: Write in detail the causes of the backwardness of the Trade and Commerce sectors in Pakistan just after independence?
a: Answers: The backwardness of Trade and Commerce The Department of Trade and Commerce was notably very backward; when Pakistan came into being. There were many causes of it, e.g. the country being agriculturist; the people were, professionally, inclined toward cultivation. They had neither experience nor capital for trade. Ultimately they used to earn their living through agriculture. Secondly, the British were responsible to end the Muslim Rule in India. They were of the opinion that Muslims were their strongest rivals. That is why they did not like the Muslims to be prosperous in any way. Another cause of the backwardness of trade was that India was the raw material supplier to England for her factories. Had the people of the sub-continent turned to trade; the factories in England would have been closed, at least. On the other hand, it was against the British policy to establish Indian Muslims economically, because the British Government was in search of strong and brave people, for the stability and extension of her rule in South Asia. They found them in Punjab. N.W.F.P., Sindh, Baluchistan, and Bengal also. The people of these provinces were brave, dutiful, dashing, and great fighters. Unfortunately, they were poor too. The British succeeded in recruiting them for defense services. The other causes were that the Hindu traders and capitalists migrated to India. The Indian refugees were educated and skilled but penniless. Due to all these causes, the department of trade and commerce remained backward for many years, after independence.

q: What is meant by per capita income?
a: Answers: Per-capita Income Per capita income means the income per head over the population of a country during a year. Formula Per capita income = net national income/population of the country Example Suppose, the population of Pakistan is 220 million and the net national income is Rs.60000 billion. So, per capita income = 60,000,000,000,000/ 220,000,000 = Rs.272000 per annual Result The increase and decrease in per capita income has functional relation with the national income of a country. It reveals the progress, prosperity, and standard of living of people.

q: Write down the causes of low per capita income in Pakistan?
a: Answers: Causes of low per capita income in Pakistan Inheritance of all economic sectors in poor condition. Agriculture yield per acre is low. Twenty-five percent of cultivable land is not being utilized. Eighty percent of our land is full of minerals but is not being utilized properly. Industrial sector is underdeveloped due to a lack of capital and capital goods. Export of raw material and finished goods need proper planning. Mostly trained and skilled laborers leave for foreign countries. Growth of population hampers, growth of per capita income. The weakest transportation system has no functional relationship with the best communication system. Per capita income would definitely increase if transportation and communication go hand in hand. A sound and transparent taxes system is liable to increase national income, as well as per capita income.
